upsertPapers.title: Near-Optimal Deterministic Network Decomposition and Ruling Set, and Improved MIS
upsertPapers.verificationNote: The deterministic theorem includes degree+1 lists. The randomized corollary states ordinary Δ+1 coloring through CLP shattering; preserve that stated contract.

upsertPapers.title: Near-Optimal Distributed Degree+1 Coloring
upsertPapers.verificationNote: Theorem 1 colors a high-degree subset with local failure Δ^{-c}; setting the degree upper bound to n yields simultaneous high-degree coverage. Theorem 2 completes all vertices.

upsertPapers.title: Distributed (Δ+1)-Coloring in Sublogarithmic Rounds
upsertPapers.verificationNote: Randomized Δ+1-list coloring; retains the exact degree-dependent historical formula.

upsertPapers.title: Distributed (Δ+1)-Coloring via Ultrafast Graph Shattering
upsertPapers.verificationNote: Randomized Δ+1-list coloring reduces to deterministic degree+1-list coloring on polylogarithmic-size graphs. Keep Det_d symbolic rather than assigning an invented exponent.

upsertPapers.title: Deterministic Distributed Vertex Coloring: Simpler, Faster, and without Network Decomposition
upsertPapers.verificationNote: The LOCAL deterministic bound applies to degree+1 lists. The randomized corollary states ordinary Δ+1 coloring with global high probability.

upsertPapers.title: Ultrafast Distributed Coloring of High Degree Graphs
upsertPapers.verificationNote: Full Δ+1-list coloring requires maximum degree at least log^{2+δ}n for fixed δ>0. Theorem is stronger CONGEST. HKNT22 incorporates this report's LOCAL work; do not count it as an independent frontier.

upsertPapers.title: Sublogarithmic Distributed Vertex Coloring with Optimal Number of Colors
upsertPapers.verificationNote: Sufficiently large Δ; q≥Δ−k_Δ+1. Output is a valid q-coloring or a local non-colorability certificate. The exceptional Δ≥log^{50}n regime is faster. No imported boundary hardness.

upsertPapers.title: Locality in Distributed Graph Algorithms
upsertPapers.verificationNote: Three-coloring an n-cycle takes at least (log* n−3)/2 rounds. Use only the deterministic case here, even with a consistent orientation. No all-degree/palette lower projection.

upsertPapers.title: A Distributed Palette Sparsification Theorem
upsertPapers.verificationNote: Communication is restricted to the sampled-color conflict network. The lower bound holds on sampled cliques even at success 2/3; explicit sampling is Bernoulli f(n)/n with c log n≤f(n)≤polylog n.

upsertPapers.title: Distributed (Δ+1)-Coloring in Linear (in Δ) Time
upsertPapers.verificationNote: Full journal theorem confirms O(Δ)+(1/2)log* n rounds for ordinary Δ+1 coloring. Specializing Δ=2 supplies the cycle upper in the reference inset.

upsertPapers.title: Local Conflict Coloring
upsertPapers.verificationNote: Set conflict degree d=1 in Theorem 4.1: lists of size degree(v)+1 suffice; exact bound is O(√Δ log^{5/2}Δ)+log* n.
